newsitem.title: USA: Detroit Ed says Mich. power system strained.
newsitem.headline: Detroit Ed says Mich. power system strained.

text.p: Hot weather and soaring power demand Monday across southern Michigan prompted Detroit Edison to ask its electricity customers to conserve power usage.
"The extreme temperatures and resulting power demand in the entire Midwest have strained the utility's ability to meet customer needs," the company said in a statement.
Temperatures in Detroit this afternoon hit a high of 94 degrees Fahrenheit.

Detroit Edison, the utility subsidiary of DTE Energy Co, said it expects electricity demand on its system to set a record this afternoon, surpassing the current record of 10,337 megawatts (MW) set August 7, 1996.
The utility asked consumers to limit air conditioning and turn off all unnecessary lights and appliances "to avoid the need to take more drastic action."
Detroit Edison's plea follows a similar request from neighboring CMS Energy Corp, based in Jackson, Mich.
CMS reported earlier Monday that electricity demand from the 9.5 million Michigan residents it serves peaked today at 7,304 MW, a record for its power system.
